- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overreacts; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to avoid immediate peak.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In low-sentiment periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 sentiment), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for subdued market behavior.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 3% from model in 3+ consecutive days, apply a “sentiment-weighted smoothing” rule: average with prior 7-day true value if sentiment is neutral or negative.
